query: A review of Colombia says that under an adverse growth shock its general government gross debt would reach 60.9 percent of GDP in 2030. Is that correct to within five percentage points? Take the IMF World Economic Outlook (October 2025) projections as the baseline and treat it as a country with access to international capital markets.

text.text: Identifies the standardized public DSA stress tests of the IMF (2013) Staff Guidance Note for Public DSA in Market-Access Countries (also MAC SRDSF 2021) and applies the growth shock: real GDP growth one standard deviation (ten-year history) below baseline for two consecutive years, revenue ratio unchanged and non-interest spending level held at baseline, +25 bp interest per 1 pp of GDP deterioration of the deficit, inflation 0.25 pp lower per 1 pp lower growth.
text.accept: full = names the standardized stress tests and applies the stated size and links; partial = right test with a different size (for example a flat 1 point shock) or without the primary-balance, interest or inflation links; no = ad hoc sensitivity, a debt-stabilising balance or a stochastic fan chart.

text.text: Judges the statement incorrect: the stated 60.9% is the unstressed baseline, and the growth shock raises 2030 debt well above it (about 68 to 74% depending on whether the 25 bp interest link is applied).

data.text: Uses WEO October 2025 general government gross debt, real GDP growth, GDP deflator, primary balance, overall balance (to derive interest) and revenue (WEO: GGXWDG_NGDP, NGDP_RPCH, NGDP_D, GGXONLB_NGDP, GGXCNL_NGDP, GGR_NGDP).
data.accept: full = debt, growth, deflator and fiscal balances all used; partial = a subset with an assumed interest rate; no = other series.

computation.text: Colombia: stressed 2030 debt is clearly above the stated 60.9% (which equals the baseline itself); defensible readings of the growth shock give about 68 to 74% of GDP.
computation.accept: full = a stressed value of at least 66; partial = above the baseline but below 66; no = at or below the baseline. The size depends on whether the 25 bp interest link is applied (68 without, 74 with); the document applies it by default.

grading.note: Stressed 2030 debt in percent of GDP. Tolerance 4 pp because the pass-through of the interest shock and the sample for the standard deviation are loose (new-issuance-only pass-through lowers the 2030 effect by several points; dropping the 25 bp link changes it by under 1 pp). Baseline reproduced from WEO Oct 2025 (gold 60.9 vs WEO 60.9).

provenance.method_text: IMF (2013) Staff Guidance Note for Public DSA in Market-Access Countries, para 29-32 and shock table; MAC SRDSF (2021)

published_value_note: No published number: stressed paths appear only in charts of country DSAs and the guidance note's example is a fictional country. Tier is definition-validated.
distractors: Debt-stabilising primary balance or required adjustment (no shock applied)
Decomposition of past changes in the debt ratio
Stress tests of the low-income country debt framework (different shocks and thresholds)
Stochastic fan chart or probabilistic debt projection (random draws; the guidance's deterministic stress tests are not fan charts)
Gross financing needs projection (liquidity flow rather than debt stock)
Ad hoc sensitivity such as a uniform 1 percentage point change in growth or in the interest rate
Fiscal multiplier analysis of a consolidation

strictness.overall: strict shock sizes, loose pass-through and standard-deviation sample

parameters.growth_shock_size: strict: real GDP growth lower by one standard deviation of its past ten-year history for two consecutive years; the gold uses the population standard deviation of 2016-2025 growth (loose sample)
parameters.growth_shock_links: strict (document Table 3): revenue-to-GDP ratio unchanged, non-interest spending LEVEL kept at the baseline, so the spending ratio rises with the cumulative GDP shortfall during the two shock years (the document's own example shows primary balance down 0.5 and 1.1 points in the two shock years, which this level effect reproduces: 29 x 1.9 percent = 0.56 and 29 x 3.7 percent = 1.07) and back at the baseline from year 3; +25 bp on the interest rate per 1 pp of GDP worsening of the deficit; inflation 0.25 pp lower per 1 pp lower growth
parameters.interest_shock_size: strict: nominal rate up by the larger of 200 bp and (highest real rate in the last ten years minus average projected real rate)
parameters.interest_shock_pass_through: loose: the document says the nominal interest rate increases by the shock size, but its example table shows the effective rate rising gradually (about 0.5, 0.8, 1.3, 1.4 points over four years); the gold applies the whole shock to the effective rate from 2026 (upper bound); a gradual pass-through (25, 40, 65, 70, 75 percent) lowers the 2030 debt by 2.1 to 4.6 points (see doc_check)
parameters.combined_shock: strict (document para 32): the combined shock takes the largest effect of the individual shocks on each variable (growth, inflation, primary balance, interest rate), without double counting; the gold takes the growth leg for growth, inflation and primary balance, and for the interest rate the larger of the 200 bp-type interest shock and the 25 bp link, not their sum
parameters.exchange_rate_shock: omitted (needs real-exchange-rate overvaluation, not a frozen series); the questions do not ask for it
parameters.baseline: strict: IMF WEO October 2025 projections 2025-2030, reproduced exactly by a stock-flow residual
parameters.review_flag: Document check against 2dea3fb1 Staff Guidance Note (blocks 136-138 Table 3, 153-154 example tables, 157 para 32): shock sizes (growth -1 SD 2 years; interest max(200 bp, max real rate 10y minus mean projected real rate); primary balance, exchange rate not used), links (25 bp per 1 pp, inflation 0.25) and the combined rule MATCH; spending-ratio persistence resolved (none after shock years); interest pass-through not defined in text (loose).
